subject: Pairs: standardize option wording so grammar isn't a tell (Ethan's call)
body: Ethan (2026-11-15): wording/grammar must not let a model tell his option from the decoy. Today render_pair rewrites both in one call but labels them 'Decision' and 'Alternative', so the rewriter knows which is real, and only length (20%) and names are checked. Asked for, before the pairs stage runs: (1) BLIND REWRITE: give the rewriter the two options shuffled as 'Option 1/Option 2' with no hint which was taken; map back by the stored shuffle. (2) FIXED TEMPLATE for both options: one sentence, imperative, present tense, no first person ('we'), no hedges, no paper-specific numbers or method names unless both options carry the same kind. Context in neutral third person. (3) CODE CHECKS in check_pair: one sentence each; digits in both or neither; no first-person pronouns in options; keep the length and name checks. (4) STYLE-LEAK PROBE beside the distractor gate: a blind judge asked 'which option was paraphrased from a published paper and which was invented?' on held-out pairs, paired-order scored; report the rate in gate_timesplit and flag it if well above chance. Applies to all researchers (Hobbhahn, Owain Evans). Files: autoresearch/taste/timesplit.py (PAIR_PROMPT, render_pair, check_pair), track_eval.py (probe), tests/test_timesplit.py, docs/track-s-extraction.md. You hold the locks and have uncommitted edits in timesplit.py, so I did not touch them. Pair with my earlier message dropping own_future_work.
